sanskrit: atra gāthā yajñagītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ vaikhānasānāṃ rājendra munīnāṃ yaṣṭum icchatām
english: On this matter, O lord of kings, those versed in ancient lore recite the verses sung of sacrifice, concerning the Vaikhānasa sages who longed to perform the rite.

sanskrit: udite 'nudite vāpi śraddadhāno jitendriyaḥ vahniṃ juhoti dharmeṇa śraddhā vai kāraṇaṃ mahat
english: Whether the sun has risen or not yet risen, the man of faith, his senses subdued, pours the oblation into the fire according to dharma; for faith, indeed, is the great cause.

sanskrit: yat skannam asya tat pūrvaṃ yad askannaṃ tad uttaram bahūni yajñarūpāṇi nānākarmaphalāni ca
english: Whatever of his oblation has spilled is reckoned the lesser, and whatever has not spilled the higher; manifold are the forms of sacrifice and varied the fruits of its diverse acts.

sanskrit: tāni yaḥ saṃvijānāti jñānaniścayaniścitaḥ dvijātiḥ śraddhayopetaḥ sa yaṣṭuṃ puruṣo 'rhati
english: He who comprehends these rites fully, firm in the certainty of knowledge, a twice-born endowed with faith—that man is fit to perform the sacrifice.

sanskrit: steno vā yadi vā pāpo yadi vā pāpakṛttamaḥ yaṣṭum icchati yajñaṃ yaḥ sādhum eva vadanti tam
english: Be he a thief, or wicked, or even the worst of evildoers—if he desires to perform the sacrifice, they call him a good man even so.

sanskrit: ṛṣayas taṃ praśaṃsanti sādhu caitad asaṃśayam sarvathā sarvavarṇair hi yaṣṭavyam iti niścayaḥ na hi yajñasamaṃ kiṃ cit triṣu lokeṣu vidyate
english: The seers praise him, and this is good beyond all doubt; for it is settled that by every means and by men of all varṇas the sacrifice must be performed—since nothing equal to sacrifice is found in the three worlds.

sanskrit: tasmād yaṣṭavyam ity āhuḥ puruṣeṇānasūyatā śraddhāpavitram āśritya yathāśakti prayacchatā
english: Therefore they declare that a man free of envy must sacrifice, taking refuge in the purity of faith and giving according to his means.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca āśramāṇāṃ mahābāho śṛṇu satyaparākrama caturṇām iha varṇānāṃ karmāṇi ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear now, O mighty-armed one of true valour, of the four stages of life and of the duties of the four varṇas, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vānaprasthaṃ bhaikṣacaryāṃ gārhasthyaṃ ca mahāśramam brahmacaryāśramaṃ prāhuś caturthaṃ brāhmaṇair vṛtam
english: The forest-dweller's life, the mendicant's begging, and householdership—that great stage—and the stage of studentship: this fourth they call the order embraced by brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: jaṭākaraṇasaṃskāraṃ dvijātitvam avāpya ca ādhānādīni karmāṇi prāpya vedam adhītya ca
english: Having undergone the rite of the matted lock and attained the state of the twice-born, having taken up the rites beginning with the kindling of the sacred fire, and having studied the Veda—

sanskrit: sadāro vāpy adāro vā ātmavān saṃyatendriyaḥ vānaprasthāśramaṃ gacchet kṛtakṛtyo gṛhāśramāt
english: whether with a wife or without one, self-possessed and with senses restrained, having discharged his obligations he may pass from the householder's stage into the forest-dweller's order.

sanskrit: tatrāraṇyakaśāstrāṇi samadhītya sa dharmavit ūrdhvaretāḥ prajāyitvā gacchaty akṣarasātmatām
english: There, having mastered the forest treatises, that knower of dharma, with seed drawn upward, having begotten offspring, attains oneness with the Imperishable.

sanskrit: etāny eva nimittāni munīnām ūrdhvaretasām kartavyānīha vipreṇa rājann ādau vipaścitā
english: These very observances of the sages of upward-drawn seed are what the learned brāhmaṇa must first perform here, O king.

sanskrit: caritabrahmacaryasya brāhmaṇasya viśāṃ pate bhaikṣacaryāsv adhīkāraḥ praśasta iha mokṣiṇaḥ
english: For the brāhmaṇa who has fulfilled his studentship, O lord of peoples, fitness for the mendicant's life is commended here, for one bound on liberation.

sanskrit: yatrāstamitaśāyī syān niragnir aniketanaḥ yathopalabdhajīvī syān munir dānto jitendriyaḥ
english: There he should sleep wherever the sun sets him, without sacred fire, without a home, living on whatever he chances to find—a sage, controlled, his senses conquered.

sanskrit: nirāśīḥ syāt sarvasamo nirbhogo nirvikāravān vipraḥ kṣemāśramaṃ prāpto gacchaty akṣarasātmatām
english: Free of craving, the same toward all, without enjoyments, unaltered—the brāhmaṇa, having reached this stage of peace, attains oneness with the Imperishable.

sanskrit: adhītya vedān kṛtasarvakṛtyaḥ; saṃtānam utpādya sukhāni bhuktvā samāhitaḥ pracared duścaraṃ taṃ; gārhasthyadharmaṃ munidharmadṛṣṭam
english: Having studied the Vedas and discharged every duty, having begotten offspring and tasted his pleasures, let him, composed, pursue that hard-to-tread dharma of householdership, beheld in the law of the sages.

sanskrit: svadāratuṣṭa ṛtukālagāmī; niyogasevī naśaṭho najihmaḥ mitāśano devaparaḥ kṛtajñaḥ; satyo mṛduś cānṛśaṃsaḥ kṣamāvān
english: Content with his own wife, approaching her in her season, observing his appointed duties, neither false nor crooked, sparing in food, devoted to the gods, grateful, truthful, gentle, free of cruelty, and forbearing—

sanskrit: dānto vidheyo havyakavye 'pramatto; annasya dātā satataṃ dvijebhyaḥ amatsarī sarvaliṅgipradātā; vaitānanityaś ca gṛhāśramī syāt
english: controlled, obedient, heedful in offerings to gods and ancestors, ever a giver of food to the twice-born, free of envy, giving to all who wear the marks of an order, and constant in the three sacred fires—such should the householder be.

sanskrit: athātra nārāyaṇagītam āhur; maharṣayas tāta mahānubhāvāḥ mahārtham atyarthatapaḥprayuktaṃ; tad ucyamānaṃ hi mayā nibodha
english: And on this, my son, the great seers of mighty soul recite the Song of Nārāyaṇa, weighty in meaning and fraught with the highest austerity; mark it well as I declare it.

sanskrit: satyārjavaṃ cātithipūjanaṃ ca; dharmas tathārthaś ca ratiś ca dāre niṣevitavyāni sukhāni loke; hy asmin pare caiva mataṃ mamaitat
english: Truth and uprightness, the honouring of guests, dharma and wealth, and delight in one's wife—these are the joys to be cultivated, in this world and the next alike: such is my view.

sanskrit: bharaṇaṃ putradārāṇāṃ vedānāṃ pāraṇaṃ tathā satāṃ tam āśramaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vadanti paramarṣayaḥ
english: The maintenance of sons and wife, and likewise the full recitation of the Vedas—that stage of the virtuous the supreme seers declare the most excellent.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi yo brāhmaṇo yajñaśīlo; gārhasthyam adhyāvasate yathāvat gṛhasthavṛttiṃ praviśodhya samyak; svarge viṣuddhaṃ phalam āpnute saḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa who, devoted to sacrifice, thus dwells duly in householdership, having purified well the householder's way of life, attains in heaven a stainless fruit.

sanskrit: tasya dehaparityāgād iṣṭāḥ kāmākṣayā matāḥ ānantyāyopatiṣṭhanti sarvatokṣiśiromukhāḥ
english: At his laying down of the body, his cherished, undecaying desires are deemed to wait upon him, leading to the infinite—beings with eyes, heads, and faces on every side.

sanskrit: khādann eko japann ekaḥ sarpann eko yudhiṣṭhira ekasminn eva ācārye śuśrūṣur malapaṅkavān
english: Eating alone, reciting alone, moving alone, O Yudhiṣṭhira, serving but one teacher, covered with the grime of penance—

sanskrit: brahmacārī vratī nityaṃ nityaṃ dīkṣāparo vaśī avicārya tathā vedaṃ kṛtyaṃ kurvan vaset sadā
english: the student, ever vowed, ever bent on consecration, self-mastered, should dwell always doing his appointed task and reciting the Veda without questioning.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣāṃ satataṃ kurvan guroḥ saṃpraṇameta ca ṣaṭkarmasv anivṛttaś ca napravṛttaś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Rendering constant service, let him bow low before his teacher, neither wholly withdrawn from the six prescribed acts nor wholly given over to them.

sanskrit: na caraty adhikāreṇa sevitaṃ dviṣato na ca eṣo ''śramapadas tāta brahmacāriṇa iṣyate
english: He does not act beyond his sanctioned office, nor serve one who is hostile: this, my son, is held to be the proper station of the student.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śivān sukhān mahodarkān ahiṃsrāṃl lokasaṃmatān brūhi dharmān sukhopāyān madvidhānāṃ sukhāvahān
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Tell me of those duties—auspicious, pleasant, of great consequence, free of harm, approved by the world, easy of means, and bringing happiness to such as I am.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca brāhmaṇasyeha catvāra āśramā vihitāḥ prabho varṇās tān anuvartante trayo bharatasattama
english: Bhīṣma said: For the brāhmaṇa, O lord, four stages of life are ordained here; the three other varṇas follow after them, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: uktāni karmāṇi bahūni rājan; svargyāṇi rājanyaparāyaṇāni nemāni dṛṣṭāntavidhau smṛtāni; kṣātre hi sarvaṃ vihitaṃ yathāvat
english: Many heaven-winning duties have been declared, O king, that have the kṣatriya for their mainstay; these are not recorded among matters of illustration, for in the warrior's code everything is ordained in due order.

sanskrit: kṣātrāṇi vaiśyāni ca sevamānaḥ; śaudrāṇi karmāṇi ca brāhmaṇaḥ san asmiṃl loke nindito mandacetāḥ; pare ca loke nirayaṃ prayāti
english: A man who, being a brāhmaṇa, takes to the works of the kṣatriya, the vaiśya, and the śūdra is censured in this world as dull of mind, and in the next world he goes to hell.

sanskrit: yā saṃjñā vihitā loke dāse śuni vṛke paśau vikarmaṇi sthite vipre tāṃ saṃjñāṃ kuru pāṇḍava
english: The name appointed in the world for a slave, a dog, a wolf, or a beast—that very name apply, O Pāṇḍava, to a brāhmaṇa settled in forbidden work.

sanskrit: ṣaṭkarmasaṃpravṛttasya āśrameṣu caturṣv api sarvadharmopapannasya saṃbhūtasya kṛtātmanaḥ
english: For one engaged in the six prescribed acts in all four stages of life, endowed with every duty, fully formed, his self perfected—

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasya viśuddhasya tapasy abhiratasya ca nirāśiṣo vadānyasya lokā hy akṣarasaṃjñitāḥ
english: for such a purified brāhmaṇa, delighting in austerity, free of craving and bountiful, the worlds are those named Imperishable.

sanskrit: yo yasmin kurute karma yādṛśaṃ yena yatra ca tādṛśaṃ tādṛśenaiva sa guṇaṃ pratipadyate
english: Whatever deed a man does, of whatever kind, by whatever means and wherever—of just that kind, and by just such means, does he reap its quality.

sanskrit: vṛddhyā kṛṣivaṇiktvena jīvasaṃjīvanena ca vettum arhasi rājendra svādhyāyagaṇitaṃ mahat
english: Through usury, through farming and trade, and through the sustaining of life, you ought to understand, O lord of kings, the great reckoning measured by sacred study.

sanskrit: kālasaṃcoditaḥ kālaḥ kālaparyāyaniścitaḥ uttamādhamamadhyāni karmāṇi kurute 'vaśaḥ
english: Time, impelled by time and fixed in the cycle of time, performs of necessity its deeds—the highest, the lowest, and the middling.

sanskrit: antavanti pradānāni purā śreyaskarāṇi ca svakarmanirato loko hy akṣaraḥ sarvatomukhaḥ
english: Finite are the gifts and the meritorious acts of old; but the world devoted to its own proper duty is imperishable, facing every way.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca jyākarṣaṇaṃ śatrunibarhaṇaṃ ca; kṛṣir vaṇijyā paśupālanaṃ ca śuśrūṣaṇaṃ cāpi tathārthahetor; akāryam etat paramaṃ dvijasya
english: Bhīṣma said: The drawing of the bowstring, the slaughter of foes, farming, trade, the herding of cattle, and likewise menial service for the sake of gain—all this is the gravest forbidden conduct for a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: sevyaṃ tu brahmaṣaṭkarma gṛhasthena manīṣiṇā kṛtakṛtyasya cāraṇye vāso viprasya śasyate
english: But the six sacred acts of the brāhmaṇa are to be practised by the wise householder; and for the brāhmaṇa who has discharged his duties, dwelling in the forest is commended.

sanskrit: rājapraiṣyaṃ kṛṣidhanaṃ jīvanaṃ ca vaṇijyayā kauṭilyaṃ kaulaṭeyaṃ ca kusīdaṃ ca vivarjayet
english: Service of a king, wealth from farming, livelihood by trade, crookedness, the offspring of an unchaste woman, and usury—all these he should shun.

sanskrit: śūdro rājan bhavati brahmabandhur; duścāritryo yaś ca dharmād apetaḥ vṛṣalīpatiḥ piśuno nartakaś ca; grāmapraiṣyo yaś ca bhaved vikarmā
english: A brāhmaṇa in name only, O king, becomes a śūdra—he who is ill-conducted and fallen from dharma, the husband of a low-born woman, the slanderer, the dancer, the village drudge, and the doer of forbidden work.

sanskrit: japan vedān ajapaṃś cāpi rājan; samaḥ śūdrair dāsavac cāpi bhojyaḥ ete sarve śūdrasamā bhavanti; rājann etān varjayed devakṛtye
english: Whether reciting the Vedas or not, O king, he is equal to śūdras, and like a slave he is one whose food may be taken; all these become the equals of śūdras, and them, O king, one should exclude from the rites of the gods.

sanskrit: nirmaryāde cāśane krūravṛttau; hiṃsātmake tyaktadharmasvavṛtte havyaṃ kavyaṃ yāni cānyāni rājan; deyāny adeyāni bhavanti tasmin
english: In one of unbridled appetite, of cruel ways, of violent nature, who has cast off dharma and his own proper conduct, O king, the offerings to gods and ancestors and all else that should be given become things not to be given to him.

sanskrit: tasmād dharmo vihito brāhmaṇasya; damaḥ śaucaṃ cārjavaṃ cāpi rājan tathā viprasyāśramāḥ sarva eva; purā rājan brahmaṇā vai nisṛṣṭāḥ
english: Therefore the dharma ordained for the brāhmaṇa is self-restraint, purity, and uprightness, O king; and likewise all the orders of the brāhmaṇa were in days of old sent forth by Brahmā himself.

sanskrit: yaḥ syād dāntaḥ somapa āryaśīlaḥ; sānukrośaḥ sarvasaho nirāśīḥ ṛjur mṛdur anṛśaṃsaḥ kṣamāvān; sa vai vipro netaraḥ pāpakarmā
english: He who is controlled, a drinker of the soma, noble in character, compassionate, all-enduring, free of craving, upright, gentle, without cruelty, and forbearing—he indeed is the brāhmaṇa, and not the other, the doer of evil deeds.

sanskrit: śūdraṃ vaiśyaṃ rājaputraṃ ca rājaṃl; lokāḥ sarve saṃśritā dharmakāmāḥ tasmād varṇāñ jātidharmeṣu saktān; matvā viṣṇur necchati pāṇḍuputra
english: The śūdra, the vaiśya, and the king's son, O king—all the worlds, desiring dharma, lean upon them; yet, deeming the varṇas bound fast in the duties of mere birth, Viṣṇu does not desire them, O son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: loke cedaṃ sarvalokasya na syāc; cāturvarṇyaṃ vedavādāś ca na syuḥ sarvāś cejyāḥ sarvalokakriyāś ca; sadyaḥ sarve cāśramasthā na vai syuḥ
english: And were this fourfold order of varṇas not to exist in the world for all the world, the doctrines of the Veda too would not be; nor would all the sacrifices and all the works of the world, and at once none would be established in the orders of life.

sanskrit: yaś ca trayāṇāṃ varṇānām icched āśramasevanam kartum āśramadṛṣṭāṃś ca dharmāṃs tāñ śṛṇu pāṇḍava
english: And he among the three varṇas who would wish to follow the orders of life and to perform the duties prescribed for those orders—hear of them, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣākṛtakṛtyasya kṛtasaṃtānakarmaṇaḥ abhyanujñāpya rājānaṃ śūdrasya jagatīpate
english: For the śūdra who has discharged his duty of service and accomplished the begetting of offspring, having gained leave of the king, O lord of the earth—

sanskrit: alpāntaragatasyāpi daśadharmagatasya vā āśramā vihitāḥ sarve varjayitvā nirāśiṣam
english: even for one who has gone but a little way, or who has gone the way of the ten duties, all the orders of life are ordained, save only that of the cravingless ascetic.

sanskrit: bhaikṣacaryāṃ na tu prāhus tasya tad dharmacāriṇaḥ tathā vaiśyasya rājendra rājaputrasya caiva hi
english: But they do not prescribe the mendicant's begging for that practiser of dharma, nor likewise for the vaiśya, O lord of kings, nor indeed for the king's son.

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyo vayotīto rājñaḥ kṛtapariśramaḥ vaiśyo gacched anujñāto nṛpeṇāśramamaṇḍalam
english: Having discharged his duties, advanced in years, and having laboured fully for the king, the vaiśya, with the king's leave, may pass into the round of the orders of life.

sanskrit: vedān adhītya dharmeṇa rājaśāstrāṇi cānagha saṃtānādīni karmāṇi kṛtvā somaṃ niṣevya ca
english: Having studied the Vedas according to dharma and the treatises on kingship, O sinless one, having performed the rites beginning with the begetting of offspring and partaken of the soma—

sanskrit: pālayitvā prajāḥ sarvā dharmeṇa vadatāṃ vara rājasūyāśvamedhādīn makhān anyāṃs tathaiva ca
english: having guarded all his subjects according to dharma, O best of speakers, having performed the Rājasūya, the Aśvamedha, and other sacrifices likewise—

sanskrit: samānīya yathāpāṭhaṃ viprebhyo dattadakṣiṇaḥ saṃgrāme vijayaṃ prāpya tathālpaṃ yadi vā bahu
english: having gathered all as prescribed and given his sacrificial fees to the brāhmaṇas, having won victory in battle, whether little or much—

sanskrit: sthāpayitvā prajāpālaṃ putraṃ rājye ca pāṇḍava anyagotraṃ praśastaṃ vā kṣatriyaṃ kṣatriyarṣabha
english: having set upon the throne, as guardian of the people, a son, O Pāṇḍava, or some other approved kṣatriya of another lineage, O bull among kṣatriyas—

sanskrit: arcayitvā pitṝn samyak pitṛyajñair yathāvidhi devān yajñair ṛṣīn vedair arcitvā caiva yatnataḥ
english: having duly honoured the ancestors with rites for the fathers according to rule, and having worshipped the gods with sacrifices and the seers with the Vedas, all with diligence—

sanskrit: antakāle ca saṃprāpte ya icched āśramāntaram ānupūrvyāśramān rājan gatvā siddhim avāpnuyāt
english: and when the end of life has come, he who would seek another order of life may, O king, passing through the orders in their due succession, attain perfection.

sanskrit: rājarṣitvena rājendra bhaikṣacaryādhvasevayā apetagṛhadharmo 'pi carej jīvitakāmyayā
english: In the manner of a royal seer, O lord of kings, by following the path of the mendicant's begging, even one who has left behind the householder's dharma may roam abroad out of his desire to live.

sanskrit: na caitan naiṣṭhikaṃ karma trayāṇāṃ bharatarṣabha caturṇāṃ rājaśārdūla prāhur āśramavāsinām
english: Yet this is not the final, perfected work of the three—nor of the four orders of those who dwell in the stages of life, O tiger among kings, so they declare, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bahv āyattaṃ kṣatriyair mānavānāṃ; lokaśreṣṭhaṃ dharmam āsevamānaiḥ sarve dharmāḥ sopadharmās trayāṇāṃ; rājño dharmād iti vedāc chṛṇomi
english: Much depends on the kṣatriyas, who practise the dharma highest among men in the world; all the duties of the three varṇas, together with their subsidiary duties, derive from the dharma of the king—so I hear from the Veda.

sanskrit: yathā rājan hastipade padāni; saṃlīyante sarvasattvodbhavāni evaṃ dharmān rājadharmeṣu sarvān; sarvāvasthaṃ saṃpralīnān nibodha
english: As, O king, within the footprint of an elephant the tracks of all creatures born are merged, so know that all the duties, in every state, are wholly merged within the duties of the king.

sanskrit: alpāśrayān alpaphalān vadanti; dharmān anyān dharmavido manuṣyāḥ mahāśrayaṃ bahukalyāṇarūpaṃ; kṣātraṃ dharmaṃ netaraṃ prāhur āryāḥ
english: Men learned in dharma call the other duties of small support and small fruit; but the noble declare that the kṣatriya's dharma, of great support and abounding in blessings, is foremost, and not another.

sanskrit: sarve dharmā rājadharmapradhānāḥ; sarve dharmāḥ pālyamānā bhavanti sarvatyāgo rājadharmeṣu rājaṃs; tyāge cāhur dharmam agryaṃ purāṇam
english: All duties have the king's dharma for their chief; by it are all duties protected; in the king's dharma lies the renouncing of all things, O king, and in renunciation, they say, lies the foremost and most ancient dharma.

sanskrit: majjet trayī daṇḍanītau hatāyāṃ; sarve dharmā na bhaveyur viruddhāḥ sarve dharmāś cāśramāṇāṃ gatāḥ syuḥ; kṣātre tyakte rājadharme purāṇe
english: Were the science of governance destroyed, the threefold Veda would sink, all duties would fall into confusion and cease to be, and all the duties of the orders of life would be undone, were the kṣatriya's ancient royal dharma forsaken.

sanskrit: sarve tyāgā rājadharmeṣu dṛṣṭāḥ; sarvā dīkṣā rājadharmeṣu coktāḥ sarve yogā rājadharmeṣu coktāḥ; sarve lokā rājadharmān praviṣṭāḥ
english: All renunciations are seen within the king's dharma; all consecrations are declared within the king's dharma; all disciplines are declared within the king's dharma; all the worlds have entered into the king's dharma.

sanskrit: yathā jīvāḥ prakṛtau vadhyamānā; dharmāśritānām upapīḍanāya evaṃ dharmā rājadharmair viyuktāḥ; sarvāvasthaṃ nādriyante svadharmam
english: As living beings, struck down in the realm of nature, serve to oppress those who hold to dharma, so the duties, sundered from the king's dharma, in no condition uphold their own proper law.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca cāturāśramyadharmāś ca jātidharmāś ca pāṇḍava lokapālottarāś caiva kṣātre dharme vyavasthitāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: The duties of the four orders of life and the duties of birth, O Pāṇḍava, and those that have the guardians of the worlds for their height, are all established within the kṣatriya's dharma.

sanskrit: sarvāṇy etāni dharmāṇi kṣātre bharatasattama nirāśiṣo jīvaloke kṣātre dharme vyavasthitāḥ
english: All these duties rest in the kṣatriya's code, O best of the Bharatas; in the world of the living, the cravingless too are established within the kṣatriya's dharma.

sanskrit: apratyakṣaṃ bahudvāraṃ dharmam āśramavāsinām prarūpayanti tadbhāvam āgamair eva śāśvatam
english: The dharma of those who dwell in the orders of life is unseen and of many gates; its nature they expound as eternal, by scriptural tradition alone.

sanskrit: apare vacanaiḥ puṇyair vādino lokaniścayam aniścayajñā dharmāṇām adṛṣṭānte pare ratāḥ
english: Others, disputants, with holy words declare a settled doctrine of the world; not knowing the certainties of the duties, they take their delight in what has no demonstrable end.

sanskrit: pratyakṣasukhabhūyiṣṭham ātmasākṣikam acchalam sarvalokahitaṃ dharmaṃ kṣatriyeṣu pratiṣṭhitam
english: But the dharma that abounds in manifest happiness, that has the self for its witness, that is free of deceit and is the good of all the world—that is firmly established among the kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: dharmāśramavyavasināṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira yathā trayāṇāṃ varṇānāṃ saṃkhyātopaśrutiḥ purā rājadharmeṣv anupamā lokyā sucaritair iha
english: As for the brāhmaṇas who abide in the dharma of the orders of life, O Yudhiṣṭhira, and likewise for the three other varṇas, the teaching reckoned of old, peerless in the duties of kingship, has been won here through good conduct, and leads to the worlds.

sanskrit: udāhṛtaṃ te rājendra yathā viṣṇuṃ mahaujasam sarvabhūteśvaraṃ devaṃ prabhuṃ nārāyaṇaṃ purā jagmuḥ subahavaḥ śūrā rājāno daṇḍanītaye
english: It has been told to you, O lord of kings, how in days of old very many valiant kings resorted to Viṣṇu of mighty splendour, the god lord of all beings, the sovereign Nārāyaṇa, for the sake of the science of governance.

sanskrit: ekaikam ātmanaḥ karma tulayitvāśrame purā rājānaḥ paryupātiṣṭhan dṛṣṭāntavacane sthitāḥ
english: Each weighing one by one his own deeds in his station, the kings of old waited reverently upon him, abiding by his word of illustration.

sanskrit: sādhyā devā vasavaś cāśvinau ca; rudrāś ca viśve marutāṃ gaṇāś ca sṛṣṭāḥ purā ādidevena devā; kṣātre dharme vartayante ca siddhāḥ
english: The Sādhyas, the gods, the Vasus and the two Aśvins, the Rudras, the All-gods, and the hosts of the Maruts—gods created of old by the First God—these perfected ones too conduct themselves within the kṣatriya's dharma.

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi dharmam arthaviniścayam nirmaryāde vartamāne dānavaikāyane kṛte babhūva rājā rājendra māndhātā nāma vīryavān
english: On this I shall set forth for you a dharma that is the settling of right purpose. When all bounds had been broken and the cause of the Dānavas alone prevailed, there was a king, O lord of kings, named Māndhātā, mighty in valour.

sanskrit: purā vasumatīpālo yajñaṃ cakre didṛkṣayā anādimadhyanidhanaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prati
english: Long ago that guardian of the earth, out of a longing to behold him, performed a sacrifice directed toward the god Nārāyaṇa, who is without beginning, middle, or end.
